method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited texts with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; the Regulations' Schedules 1-3 as tables (voca-schedules.l4), a seat-neutral core (voca-core.l4, with six regulative rules: ss 29, 45, 46(10), 47F; ss 47, 47G; s 46(1) and (4); ss 47C and 47E(1); ss 47H(2)(b) and 47J; s 47K, the last clocked from the date of the closure) and three seat layers (voca-seat.l4, voca-seat-funeral.l4, voca-seat-levy.l4) that call the core for every rule; no REFUSE (a Schedule 3 item that is not a leaf of the table answers `not covered`, asserted); checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. Fixed on 24 October 2026 after an independent verification (NOTES.md findings 23-26). No pipeline, no coverage table, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Victims of Crime Assistance Act 2006 (NT), reprint REPV014, as in force at 1 July 2025 (../../registers/source-bundle/Victims-of-Crime-Assistance-Act-2006-NT-current-reprint-REPV014.txt), s 61 as amended by Act No. 12 of 2025 from 1 July 2025; with the Victims of Crime Assistance Regulations 2007 (NT), reprint REPV014R1, as in force at 25 March 2024 (subjects/au/nt/victims-of-crime-assistance-regulations-2007/registers/source-bundle/Victims-of-Crime-Assistance-Regulations-2007-NT-current-reprint-REPV014R1.txt); both unofficial copies from legislation.nt.gov.au

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run voca-schedules.l4 ; l4 run voca-core.l4 ; l4 run voca-seat.l4 ; l4 run voca-seat-funeral.l4 ; l4 run voca-seat-levy.l4 ; l4 run voca-cases-victim.l4 ; l4 run voca-cases-funeral.l4 ; l4 run voca-cases-levy.l4
checks.result: 286 assertions satisfied (221 in voca-cases-victim.l4, 40 in voca-cases-funeral.l4, 25 in voca-cases-levy.l4), 0 errors, 0 warnings (2026-10-24); 9 #TRACEs with an expect line (5 breaches: the Territory under ss 45, 29 and 47F, the person required to refund under ss 47 and 47G; 4 obligations pending, with no period in the Act: the assessor's decision on an increased award (s 46(4)) and on an award application kept open (ss 47H(2)(b), 34(1)), the Director's decision on funeral expense assistance (s 47E(1)) and reopening (s 47K)), each read and as expected
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: Act ss 4, 5, 6, 7 with regs 3-7 and 7A; ss 9-16 and 22 (primary, secondary, family and related victims and what each may apply for; the heads of financial loss in ss 10(5), 12(6), 14(3)); ss 17-18 with reg 13 (exclusion where a Motor Accidents (Compensation) benefit or Return to Work compensation is paid or payable for the same injury, claimed or not; the other scheme's entitlement an input; counselling stays open); s 19 (death); ss 25, 25B, 26, 27(5), 28, 29 (interim payments, $5 000, at most the loss); ss 29A, 31, 37-43 (awards: s 38 $40 000 less interim, financial loss $10 000 less interim, the $7 500 standard-amount threshold; s 39 shared cap, proportional reduction and the s 39(5)-(7) witness priority; s 40 shared cap, dependants first, s 40(8)-(9); s 41 may reduce; s 42 must reduce by payments received; s 43 must not award); regs 14-16 with Schedules 1, 2 and 3 as tables, reg 18 (100%, 30%, 15%, no more), reg 19, regs 20-22, reg 23 (loss of earnings, NT AWE an input); ss 45-46 (payment; increase, applied for within 3 years, a regulative rule); s 47 (refund, a regulative rule on the recipient, at least 28 days, a debt to the Territory); ss 47A-47G (funeral expense assistance: within 2 years of death unless the Director accepts later, a regulative rule with the Director's duty to decide; the lesser of reasonable cost net of other payments and $15 000; the s 47G refund); ss 47H-47K (closure if uncontactable: the 30 days from the notice and the 6 months from the closure as two rules); s 48 and Schedule 1 (NTCAT review; the NTCAT Act time limit an input); s 54 (no legal costs beyond reasonable disbursements); s 61(2), (3), (6)-(10) with reg 26 (the levy: who, how many revenue units, the exceptions, a part payment to the levy first, immunity only when both are paid; the value of a revenue unit an input). Out: Part 5 (recovery from offenders); s 61(4), (6)(b); reg 30; ss 21, 24, 33-36, 44, 55, 60, 62-70; regs 8-12, 24-25, 27-29, 31. Read with subjects/au/nt/return-to-work-act-1986/ and subjects/au/nt/motor-accidents-compensation-act-1979/ (the s 17 and s 18 inputs) and subjects/au/social-security-act-1991/encodings/baseline-2026-10/ (s 17(2B): an award here is not compensation under the Social Security Act); cross-folder IMPORT is not possible.
seats: the victim applying for assistance (primary, secondary, family or related victim)
the person who paid for a victim's funeral
the person on whom the s 61 levy is imposed (found guilty and not imprisoned, paying an infringement notice, or subject to an enforcement order)
